Se'if katan 4: And specifically, etc. That the oven is small, meaning that it does not hold twelve esronim of matzah, for we require that it not be a tefach thick, as below in siman 460 se'if 5. The Pri Chadash wrote in Yoreh Deah, in Kuntres Acharon, siman 97, that the floor of the oven must hold this measure; and in Pleisi, siman 108, he wrote that the sides must hold this measure, for in the days of the Sages of the Talmud they would attach the bread to its walls. The Rema wrote there that in a place of loss, meaning great loss, one may be lenient with chametz. Therefore with chametz, etc.: this the Magen Avraham wrote from his own reasoning. For one could say that in truth, if it is completely sealed, there is no distinction between chametz and other prohibitions, and in both cases we permit only in a place of great loss. The Rema did not write to be more stringent with chametz than with other prohibitions except where it is slightly open at the place where the smoke exits; in such a case, with other prohibitions it is permitted even not in a place of loss, but with chametz we require specifically this kind of great loss. There is no distinction with chametz between whether it is open at the place where the smoke exits or not. Rather, it seemed reasonable to the Magen Avraham that just as we are more stringent with chametz than with other prohibitions where it is open at the place where the smoke exits, so too one should be stringent if it is completely sealed: where with other prohibitions we permit only in a place of great loss, with chametz we go down one level and forbid even in a place of great loss.
And furthermore, Tosafos in Avodah Zarah are stringent, etc. That is, regarding chametz; see what the Shach wrote in siman 108, s.k. 13. With this the proof of Maharil is rejected. Maharil wrote in siman 186: it seems that you were uncertain, since chametz forbids by a mashehu, whether aroma is a halachic factor, etc. It appears that there is no distinction according to the one who says aroma is not a halachic factor. A proof is that Levi permitted kosher-slaughtered meat roasted with neveilah meat in every case, even where both are one type, even according to the one who says that one type with its own type forbids by a mashehu. So too it is proven there in Perek Keitzad Tzolin, where the Gemara asks, according to the view that the concern is mixture of flavors: what difference is there between kid and kid, and what difference is there between kid and lamb? Let it say not only kid and kid, which is one type with its own type, where according to Rabbi Yehuda and Rebbe, etc., one type with its own type forbids by a mashehu, but even kid and lamb, which are one type with another type. Rav too holds that one type with its own type forbids by a mashehu. End quote from Maharil. His intent is that we say in Perek Keitzad Tzolin, folio 76: it was stated, fatty kosher-slaughtered meat that one roasted with lean neveilah meat; Rav said it is forbidden. What is the reason? Aroma is a halachic factor. Levi said it is permitted; aroma is not a halachic factor. They raised an objection: one may not roast two Pesach offerings together, because of mixture. What, is this not mixture of flavors, and it is difficult for Levi? No, it is because of mixture of the bodies. The reason for mixture of their bodies or of their flavors is that through this the Pesach is eaten not by those appointed for it. The Gemara derives this from what the latter clause teaches, even a kid and a lamb. Granted, if it is because of their bodies, that is why it teaches even kid and lamb; but if it is because of mixture of flavors, what difference is there between kid and lamb and kid and kid? Rather, what, etc., mixture of flavors, and it is permitted? Let this be a refutation of Rav. End quote from the Gemara. Maharil inferred from the questioners' challenge to Rav, asking why it says even kid and lamb, for what novelty is there in kid and lamb more than in kid and kid, if the reason is mixture of flavors? If, even according to us who rule like Levi, nevertheless with chametz aroma is a halachic factor because Levi concedes that at least a mashehu exists, while Rav holds that aroma is a full flavor, then kid and lamb would indeed be a novelty: not only kid and kid, which is one type with its own type and the baraisa follows Rabbi Yehuda, who holds one type with its own type forbids by a mashehu, so that it is forbidden even if aroma is not a halachic factor, since at least a mashehu exists; but even kid and lamb, which are one type with another type, are forbidden because it is a full flavor. Rather, one must say that the Talmud holds that if aroma is a halachic factor, it is a full flavor, and if it is not a halachic factor, there is not even a mashehu of flavor. If so, it properly asks: what difference is there between kid, etc. About this Magen Avraham wrote that according to the Rif his proof is rejected. At first glance one could answer Maharil's proof: even if we say Levi concedes that at least a mashehu exists, nevertheless the Gemara properly asks what difference there is between kid, etc.; although kid and kid is one type with its own type, the baraisa is speaking initially, for it teaches, one may not roast, and regarding the initial law there is no distinction between its own type and another type. Whatever is forbidden after the fact with its own type because it forbids by a mashehu is at least initially forbidden with another type, for we hold that one may not nullify a prohibition initially. One must say that Maharil was troubled by this: Tosafos there rejected Rashi's explanation, for Rashi holds that Levi disagrees only after the fact but admits that initially it is forbidden. If so, what does the Talmud ask against Levi from the baraisa, one may not roast two Pesach offerings, since the baraisa speaks initially? Rather, perforce Levi permits even initially. Maharil would then have a difficulty according to the questioner's view, that Levi concedes that at least a mashehu exists, and therefore with chametz aroma is a halachic factor. If so, this itself is difficult: why does Levi permit initially; do we not say that one may not nullify a prohibition initially? If so, there is no challenge to Levi at all from the baraisa of one may not roast two Pesach offerings. Perforce the Talmud must hold that this is not called nullifying a prohibition, since his intent is not to nullify, as below in siman 453 se'if 3; see there in the Taz, and in Yoreh Deah siman 84, s.k. 45 in the Shach, and in many places. According to this, Maharil's proof is sound: if there is certainly a mashehu, kid and lamb would properly be a novelty, since they are not the same type, and one might have thought that aroma is only a mashehu and that even initially, with another type, it is permitted because his intent is not to nullify; therefore it teaches us that it is a full flavor. This is a proper rejection of the questioner's view according to Maharil, namely that Rav holds it is a full flavor, while Levi, whom we rule like, nevertheless holds that it is at least a mashehu of flavor. But according to the Rif, even Rav himself holds there is only a mashehu of flavor; if so, certainly according to Levi there is not even a mashehu. For if not, what is Levi's reason? Do not say it is because Levi holds that one type with its own type is nullified, for then their dispute would not depend at all on the law of whether aroma is a halachic factor, but on whether one type with its own type forbids by a mashehu or not, and they should have disputed generally about one type with its own type. Rather, perforce Levi holds that even according to the one who says one type with its own type forbids by a mashehu, aroma is nevertheless not a halachic factor, for there is not even a mashehu of flavor. The Rif, however, holds that we rule like Rav against Levi for the reasons the Rif wrote there; yet one cannot rule like Rav in this case, since Rav concedes it is only a mashehu of flavor. Rather, Rav follows his own view that one type with its own type forbids by a mashehu, and kosher-slaughtered meat with neveilah is one type with its own type. If so, for us, who hold that one type with its own type is nullified, one cannot rule like Rav in that case; but regarding chametz, where we hold that it forbids by a mashehu, we rule like Rav that aroma is a halachic factor. According to this, Maharil's proof is rejected. For according to the Rif one must say that when the Talmud asks Rav, why even kid and lamb, it should have said: if the reason is mixture of flavors, why is kid and lamb, which is one type with another type, forbidden, since even according to Rav aroma is only a mashehu? Perforce one must say that nevertheless, since the baraisa speaks regarding the initial law, as it teaches, one may not roast, etc., regarding the initial law even another type is forbidden according to Rav, because one may not nullify a prohibition initially; perforce one must say that this is called intending to nullify. Even so, it properly asks against Levi, because according to Levi it must be permitted even initially, for according to Levi there is not even a mashehu of flavor, as above. According to this, Maharil's proof is gone, for the Gemara properly asks what difference there is between kid, etc.; although one is one type with its own type and the other is another type, since the baraisa speaks initially, and regarding the initial law there is no distinction between its own type and another type, for one may not nullify a prohibition initially, as above.
In the Mordechai, etc. Rather, he proved, etc. This comes to answer the difficulty of the Shach in Yoreh Deah siman 108, s.k. 14, who wrote regarding the Rema there, and some say one should not distinguish, meaning that chametz too, regarding aroma, is equal to other prohibitions. These are the words of Darchei Moshe in the name of the Mordechai. The Shach wrote: this requires examination, for in the Mordechai, Perek Kol Shaah, it says only that aroma does not apply to chametz bread baked with matzah, because we do not find an aroma of bread with bread, etc. End quote. For this Magen Avraham wrote that the Rema was precise from the language of the Mordechai, whose words in Perek Kol Shaah, siman 570, are as follows: an incident occurred on Pesach in which a non-Jew threw a chametz cake into an oven full of matzos, etc.; but if it did not touch, it is permitted, for we hold aroma is not a halachic factor. So too Rabbeinu Tam answered, etc.: we have not found that the aroma of forbidden bread forbids permitted bread, etc. End quote. The Shach understood that the Mordechai and Rabbeinu Tam stand in one approach, permitting because the aroma of bread with bread does not forbid, but he would concede that the aroma of roasting forbids on Pesach. But Magen Avraham wrote according to the Rema's view, because the Mordechai wrote, for we hold aroma is not a halachic factor, which implies even a complete aroma. Otherwise he should have said that the aroma of bread does not forbid, as Rabbeinu Tam wrote, and he would not have written, so too Rabbeinu Tam answered, etc. Rather, Rabbeinu Tam also permitted, but not for the Mordechai's reason; Rabbeinu Tam permitted because the aroma of bread, etc., does not forbid. According to this, the Rema properly proved that according to the Mordechai there is no distinction between chametz and other prohibitions, and even with chametz, even a complete aroma is not a halachic factor. What Rabbeinu Tam wrote, that we have not found the aroma of bread, etc., implying that a complete aroma does forbid, is not because of the stringency of chametz, but because Rabbeinu Tam holds that even with other prohibitions aroma is a halachic factor, like Rav, as Magen Avraham wrote in s.k. 3. About this Magen Avraham wrote that nevertheless even in the Mordechai it is not explicit that he permits a complete aroma with chametz. Granted, his language implies this, but it can be rejected as the Shach wrote, that the Mordechai's intent is like Rabbeinu Tam: when he wrote that we hold aroma is not a halachic factor, he meant a weak aroma, like the aroma of bread with bread, where we hold it is not a halachic factor; but with a complete aroma, one may say that he concedes it forbids on Pesach, even though with other prohibitions we rule like Levi.
And here both are equal. That is to say, the Rif and Tosafos in Avodah Zarah are equal here, as written above. In any case, one should not be lenient when it is completely sealed, etc. Chok Yaakov disagrees and permits even when it is completely sealed in a case of great loss; see there.
And all this is with roasting, etc. And similar cases, where it was not entirely, etc. That is to say, since the Rema brought proof to forbid cooking from the fact that Mahariv forbade hot foods insulated for Shabbos, it seemed to him that cooking and insulating hot foods for Shabbos are the same. But according to our text in Issur VeHeter, Issur VeHeter also explicitly distinguishes between cooking and insulating hot foods for Shabbos. If so, one may say that Mahariv too permits cooking, and forbade only one who insulates for Shabbos. Perhaps the Rema also intended this, for he wrote in Yoreh Deah siman 108 regarding what the Beis Yosef wrote: when does this apply? With roasting; but if he comes to cook them in a pot, each one by itself, etc., it is permitted. About this the Rema wrote: specifically when the oven is somewhat open, but if it is closed on all sides in the way that one insulates hot foods for Shabbos, it is forbidden. End quote. His intent in writing, in the way that one insulates, etc., is not that it is merely closed on all sides, while he would hold that even if one cooked them for an hour or two it is forbidden. Rather, by writing, in the way that one insulates, etc., he means that it is both closed and remains there for a long time, and because of this there is a strong aroma, as the Magen Avraham wrote. But with cooking, the Rema concedes that it is permitted.
And although the Beis Yosef in Yoreh Deah, etc. He wrote in the name of the Rashba that the aroma of cooking does not forbid. He brought proof from the fact that we ask against Rav from the baraisa, one may not roast two Pesach offerings, etc., which must be because of mixture of their bodies, since it teaches even a kid and a lamb. This implies that for mixture of their flavors we are not concerned, because aroma is not a halachic factor, as above. Rabbi Yirmeyah answered that he roasted them in two pots. The Gemara asked: could one think two pots? A Pesach offering requires roasting by fire. It answered: something like two pots. Rashi explained: a spit from this side, etc., and a large mound of coals or ash in the middle. Since it answered, in two pots, this implies that in a pot there is no aroma, and therefore cooking does not forbid, because there is no aroma. According to this, pot-roasting is forbidden, because although it is in a pot, nevertheless there is aroma, since it is roasting. The Beis Yosef objected: according to the conclusion, something like two pots necessarily speaks of actual roasting, for it requires roasting by fire, and there is aroma, and nevertheless it is permitted; necessarily the reason is because there is a mound interrupting. So too according to the initial assumption, that he roasted them in two pots, this means pot-roasting, and there is aroma; necessarily one must say it is because there is an interruption of a pot. If so, even pot-roasting is permitted. Magen Avraham rejected this: the interruption of a pot helps according to the conclusion because there is a large mound, so that before the aroma reaches above the mound, the aroma disperses; but the interruption of a pot alone does not help, because the aroma exits upward. Also according to the initial assumption that he roasted them in two pots, it does not speak of pot-roasting, but of actual cooking, and the reason is that cooking has no aroma. About this the Gemara asks: two pots, meaning cooking, could one think so, for it requires roasting by fire? It also could have said: the baraisa teaches one may not roast, so how can you say it is cooking in two pots? Rather, one may say that this too is included in its question, two pots, could one think so, for it teaches one may not roast, etc. But when it answered that he roasted them in two pots, which according to the Magen Avraham's intent means that he cooked them in two pots, one must say that the word roasted is not precise. Since the hole is in a high place, the aroma spreads upward; see there, where he brought proof. And perhaps one may rely, etc., in a case of loss, etc. People ask: is it not obvious to him above that even if the hole is not in a high place, but it is open at the place where the smoke exits, the Rema permits above, and so the Magen Avraham agreed in a case of loss? They answer that above we require specifically great loss, as the Shach wrote; but when the hole is in a high place, then even if there is only a small loss one may be lenient.
And what the Olas Shabbos wrote, that with chametz, etc. The Rema wrote there in Yoreh Deah that if either the forbidden item or the permitted item is a sharp substance, even with other prohibitions it is forbidden. The Shach wrote: even in a large oven whose mouth is open from the side. If so, one may say that on Pesach it is forbidden even in a case of great loss. About this the Olas Shabbos wrote that with chametz we do not find that the prohibited item would be sharp. About this the Magen Avraham wrote that it can be found with borscht. The reason he did not write beer-vinegar is that he follows his own reasoning in s.k. 28, that beer-vinegar is not so much a sharp substance, as the Pleisi wrote there.

magen_avraham.he:
ויש חולקים. ולפ"ז מ"ש בס"ב דבטל בס' צריך לאוכלו קודם פסח:
בדבר יבש. כגון שנתערב חמץ במצה חד בתרי כמ"ש בס"ט צריך ג"כ לאוכלו קודם פסח משום שהחמץ בעין: ונ"ל אף על גב דלח בלח מותר לקיימו לכ"ע יבש ביבש אסור דעכ"פ החמץ בביתו וכמ"ש רס"י תמ"ב, מיהו לדעת הרא"ש שכ' בי"ד סי' ק"ט דיבש ביבש שנתערב נעשה היתר גמור ומותר אח"כ לבשלן ביחד א"כ ה"נ מותר לקיימו דנעשה היתר גמור מיהו לא קי"ל הכי אלא במקום הפסד מיהו נ"ל דהכא אם יכול לבשלו עד שיהא נימוח ויתערב קודם פסח בס' אז מותר לאכלו בפסח ואין זה מבטל איסור לכתחלה כמ"ש שם בי"ד:
אסור בפסח. ועכ"פ מותר לקיימו:
דחיישי' שמא וכו'. כ' הש"כ ול"נ דהרשב"א לטעמיה אזיל דס"ל דחוזר וניעור בפסח אבל לדידן מותר ע"י ס' כמ"ש הב"ח סי' תמ"ב ס"ה וכן נוהגין מורי הוראה עכ"ל בגליון וצ"ע דהא כשסננו ולא נשאר אלא טעם בעלמא לכ"ע אינו חוזר וניעור כמ"ש ס"ג לכן נ"ל דרמ"א כתב שנטלו משם אבל לא סיננו עד הפסח ולכן אסר אבל סיננו קודם הפסח לכ"ע שרי, מיהו במי דבש שלפעמים הם עבים אין להם תקנה ע"י סינון (ועבי"ד סי' פ"ד וסי' ק"ד) וכתב הרשב"א דלקח מאותו חבית יין לאחר שהוציא הפת ממנו ועירבו ביין אחר ואסר כול' ע"ש:
ונותנים טעם בפסח. הכא לכ"ע אסור אפי' בצונן כיון דשורה מע"ל ה"ל כבוש כמבושל:
magen_avraham.en:
Some disagree. He discusses whether nullified chametz returns and becomes forbidden on Pesach, especially in dry mixtures or where particles may remain.
in a dry matter. For example, if chametz is mixed with a sharp matzah in the Kmash of the Set, it is necessary for the Rabbi to eat it before Pesach because the chametz is in the eye: and above, even on the back of a boil, it is permissible to keep it dry in a dry place. It is permissible to maintain it, if it is a complete permit, which is not the kil most, but instead of a loss, which is the above, then if it can be cooked until it is soft and intervenes before Pesach in S, then it is permissible to eat it on Pesach and this does not invalidate the prohibition to begin with it as a mash there in 4th:
Forbidden on Pesach. He discusses whether nullified chametz returns and becomes forbidden on Pesach, especially in dry mixtures or where particles may remain.
Concern lest, etc. Shach wrote, and it appears Rashba follows his reason that it returns and revives on Pesach; but for us it is permitted through sixty, as Beit Chadash siman 442 seif 5 wrote, and so practice halachic decisors - end of his gloss. Requires study, for when they strained and only taste remains, according to all it does not return and revive, as in seif 3; therefore it appears Rama wrote that they removed the bread from there but did not strain until Pesach, and therefore he forbade; but if they strained before Pesach, according to all it is permitted. However, in mead that is sometimes thick there is no remedy through straining (and see Yoreh De'ah siman 84 and siman 104). Rashba wrote that one who took from that wine barrel after removing the bread from it and mixed it in other wine forbade all of it [see there]:
and give a taste of Pesach. This is forbidden in the cold, since it is a delicacy from the the spirit, pickled as boiled:

mishnah_berurah.he:
(כח) קודם הפסח - אפילו אחר שש:
(כט) לאסור במשהו - מעשה שנמצאת חלה אחת של בצק בתוך הסל שהיו נותנין המצות אפויות ביציאתן מן התנור והריקו הסל ולא נודע באיזה מצות נגע הבצק ופסקו הפוסקים דחד בתרי בטל כיון שהיה התערובות קודם פסח ומותר לחמם המצות בפסח כיון דליכא אלא טעמא בעלמא ומיהו כל המצות שידוע שנגעו בבצק צריכין קליפה לפי שאין ביטול לאיסור הידוע:
(ל) ויש חולקים - ולדעתם מש"כ בס"ב דבטל בששים צריך לאוכלו קודם הפסח או דמיירי שלא היה בו אלא טעמא לבד וכנ"ל באות כ':
(לא) ונוהגין כסברא הראשונה וכו' - ומותר אפילו חזרו וחממו בפסח [אחרונים]:
(לב) שהוא לח בלח - כגון שכר שנתערב ביין וכה"ג וקמח בקמח ג"כ מקרי לח בלח ועיין לקמן בסימן תנ"ג אות י"ז במ"ב כתבו האחרונים דבדבר שהוא לח בלח אפילו לא נודע התערובות עד הפסח ג"כ אמרינן דכבר נתבטל:
(לג) ומיהו בדבר יבש שנתערב - קודם פסח בין שנתערב חמץ במצה חד בתרי או שנתערב בששים ויותר אמרינן דחוזר ונעור בפסח משום שהחמץ בעין וע"כ צריך לאכלו קודם פסח. ואם היה חד בתרי אסור אף להשהות מדרבנן ואם היה ששים יכול לבשלו קודם פסח עד שיהא נימוח ויהיה חשיב כלח ואז מותר אף לאוכלו בפסח ויש כמה אחרונים שסוברין דאף יבש ביבש דאמרינן דחוזר וניעור אינו אא"כ יאפה או יבשל אותם בפסח דאז חוזר החמץ ונותן טעם בהשאר אבל לאכול כך שרי:
(לד) אע"פ שנטלו משם - ר"ל קודם הפסח:
(לה) אסור בפסח - היינו לשתותו אבל מותר בהנאה ומכ"ש דמותר לקיימו כיון שהוא רק חשש בעלמא [אחרונים]:
(לו) דחיישינן שמא וכו' - ר"ל דמשום הטעם שיש בהיין ע"י הפת שנשרה בתוכו ולא היו אוסרין דהטעם כבר נתבטל בששים קודם הפסח ואינו חוזר וניעור רק דחיישינן שמא נשארו אז פירורין בעת הנטילה ועיין באחרונים שהסכימו דלא מחמרינן אלא כשלא סיננו קודם הפסח [ואף שבפסח סיננו לא מהני דכבר נאסר ע"י הפירורין תיכף בתחלת הפסח שנתנו טעם בהיין] אבל אם סיננו שרי אף דנשרה מעל"ע [אם יש ששים ביין נגד כל הפת]. ודוקא ביין שהוא צלול ומסתנן ע"י מסננת שנקביה דקין מאד שא"א לפירורי פת לעבור דרך שם. אבל אם נפל הפת במי דבש שלפעמים הם עבים ואינו עובר אלא במסננת שנקביה אינם דקין כ"כ חיישינן שמא יעבור גם הפירורין דרך שם:
(לז) נשארו בו פירורין וכו' - ואפילו לקח קודם הפסח מאותו חבית יין לאחר שהוציא הפת ממנו ועירבו בחבית אחרת של יין ג"כ נאסר כולה דשמא נפל הפירורין גם שם:
(לח) ונותנין טעם בפסח - ואף דבצונן יש הרבה מתירים לקמן בסימן תס"ז סי"ב הכא לכו"ע אסור דמיירי שעבר מעל"ע מנפילת הפת עד עכשיו [מ"א] ולפי מה שמבואר לקמן בסימן תס"ז סי"ב במ"ב שם בשם האחרונים דאם נפל פרוסת לחם לתוך מים בפסח לכו"ע אסור משום דדרכו להתפרר ולהיות נמס בתוך המים ואפילו סינון המים לא מהני ה"נ אפילו ליכא מעל"ע מעת שנפל הפת לתוך המים ג"כ אסור אם לא שסיננו קודם הפסח דאז מה שנימס בטל בששים. אם שאב הזוהמא של מי דבש בנפה שניפו בה קמח שרי לשתותו בפסח דבטל בס' דהוי לח בלח [אחרונים]:
mishnah_berurah.en:
Before Pesach. Even after six hours.
To forbid in any amount. There was a case in which one piece of dough was found in the basket into which baked matzos were placed when they came out of the oven. They emptied the basket and it was not known which matzos the dough had touched. The poskim ruled that one against two is nullified, since the mixture occurred before Pesach, and it is permitted to heat the matzos on Pesach because there is only mere taste. However, all matzos known to have touched the dough require peeling, since there is no nullification for a known prohibition.
And some disagree. According to them, what is written in seif 2, that it is nullified in sixty, means that one must eat it before Pesach, or that it speaks where there was only taste alone, as above in letter 20.
And the practice follows the first opinion, etc. It is permitted even if they reheated it on Pesach, as the later authorities write.
For it is liquid mixed with liquid. Such as beer mixed with wine and the like. Flour mixed with flour is also considered liquid with liquid. See below, siman 453, letter 17 in the Mishnah Berurah. The later authorities wrote that with something that is liquid with liquid, even if the mixture became known only on Pesach, we also say that it had already been nullified.
However, with a dry item that became mixed. Before Pesach, whether chametz became mixed with matzah one against two, or it became mixed with sixty or more, we say that it reawakens on Pesach because the chametz is present; therefore one must eat it before Pesach. If it was one against two, it is forbidden even to keep it D’Rabbanan. If there was sixty, he may cook it before Pesach until it dissolves and is considered liquid, and then it is even permitted to eat it on Pesach. Several later authorities hold that even dry with dry, where we say it reawakens, is only when he bakes or cooks them on Pesach, for then the chametz again gives taste into the rest; but to eat it as is, it is permitted.
Although he removed it from there. Meaning, before Pesach.
It is forbidden on Pesach. This means to drink it, but it is permitted for benefit, and certainly one may keep it, since it is only a mere concern, as the later authorities write.
For we are concerned lest, etc. Meaning, because of the taste that is in the wine from the bread that soaked in it, we would not forbid, for the taste was already nullified in sixty before Pesach and does not reawaken. Rather, we are concerned that crumbs perhaps remained at the time the bread was removed. See the later authorities, who agreed that we are stringent only where he did not filter it before Pesach. Although he filtered it on Pesach, that does not help, for it already became forbidden through the crumbs immediately at the start of Pesach when they gave taste in the wine. But if he filtered it, it is permitted, even if it soaked for twenty-four hours, provided there is sixty in the wine against all the bread. This applies specifically to clear wine that is filtered through a strainer with very fine holes, so that bread crumbs cannot pass through. But if the bread fell into mead, which is sometimes thick and passes only through a strainer whose holes are not so fine, we are concerned that the crumbs may also pass through there.
Crumbs remained in it, etc. Even if one took from that barrel of wine before Pesach after removing the bread from it and mixed it into another barrel of wine, all of it is also forbidden, lest crumbs also fell there.
And they impart taste on Pesach. Although regarding cold there are many who permit below in siman 467, seif 12, here all agree that it is forbidden, for the case is where twenty-four hours passed from when the bread fell until now, as the Magen Avraham writes. According to what is explained below in siman 467, seif 12 in the Mishnah Berurah there in the name of the later authorities, that if a slice of bread fell into water on Pesach, all agree it is forbidden because its way is to crumble and dissolve in the water, and even filtering the water does not help; here too, even if twenty-four hours did not pass from when the bread fell into the water, it is forbidden unless he filtered it before Pesach, for then what dissolved was nullified in sixty. If one drew off the scum of mead with a sieve in which flour had been sifted, it is permitted to drink it on Pesach, for it is nullified in sixty, since it is liquid mixed with liquid, as the later authorities write.

netiv_chayim.he: <small>(שם כ')</small> דין צונן דאסור הבשר בשם המרדכי נ"ב פ' כל שעה סי' תקע"ב:
netiv_chayim.en: [4] <small>There, note 20.</small> The law of cold food, that the meat is forbidden in the name of Mordechai. Note: chapter Kol Sha'ah, siman 572.

peri_megadim.he:
מו׳ שעות עט״ז עד הלילה לוקין באכילה ואין כרת בטל בס׳ כ״כ הרא״ש ז״ל פסחים ל׳ עי׳ אות א׳ ונט״ל קיל ממשהו דלהמחבר בס״י מותר עט״ז תס״ו אות י״א וה״ה יבש ביבש עד הלילה אם אין דבר שבמנין עמ״א אות מ׳ ויבואר שם אי״ה וה״ה ריח עד הלילה שוה לשאר איסורין ונוקשה משמע באות י״ט דאסור במשהו משום ל״פ אטו חמץ גמור משא״כ עד הלילה גם י״ל בין נוקשה דרע לאכילה ובין לא היה מעולם כ״א הכסיפו פניו ומיהו ז״א. וביום ח׳ מותר לשהות משהו אבל בפחות מס׳ לא משמע דאסור לשהות וצ״ע דזה למ״ד בתמ״ו ס״ב י״ט ב׳ בחה״מ אבל למ״ש הח״י בתמ״ו ה׳ וא״ר ג׳ ובא״ז שם אף לא בטלו ועובר ב״י אין מבערו בי״ט ב׳ וא״כ אם נאמר ה״ה ביום ח׳ א״כ בהכרח משהה אותו ולאחר הפסח שרי אם נאמר דטכ״ע אין עובר ב״י ובאכילה אסור דחיך אוכל יטעם או למ״ד ח״ש אין עובר ב״י וכ״ש אם אין גוף החמץ קיים רק כף בלוע מחמץ ב״י ותחב לקדירה אין ששים דאפשר אף באכילה שרי לאחר הפסח ועמ״א אות מ״ב ואי״ה שם יבואר ובתס״ז יבואר עוד.ועשו״ת ח״צ סי׳ פ״ו והמ״א בתס״ז י״ד בחמץ גמור מיירי וכ״מ מהראי׳ שהביא מתמ״ח שהביא כבר יע״ש ואי״ה שם יבואר עוד:
ואם נתערב כלי חמץ בכלי פסח עמ״א אות מ׳. וראיתי שאופין קוכין חמץ בכלי אגנות נחושת או נחושת קלל או בקערות בדיל בתנור גרוף אם דזה מקרי תשמישו ע״י אור וכדבעינן למימר לקמן אי״ה בתנ״א במ״א אות כ״א אם כן בע״פ בנחושת יש להחמיר דהא יוכל ללבן משא״כ בבדיל דא״א בליבון דניתך לא הוי דשיל״מ ושרי אם נתערב עד הלילה קערה חמץ כה״ג עם קערות פסח ואם נאבד אחת כולם הותרו אף תוך הפסח עסי׳ תס״ז במ״א ד׳ ודוקא אבוד מן העולם. ואם נתערב קערה חמץ כ״ר עד הלילה יש להגעיל א׳ מהם והותרו כולם דהוי כשהשליך א׳ לים ועדיין היתר הוא דעד הלילה בטל ברוב הוא ומיהו למאן דמחמיר באות מ׳ יצויר זה בנחושת באור ע״י ליבון ואי״ה במ״ד יבואר עוד במ״א. עסי׳ תנ״ג במ״א אות ג׳ וסוף הסימן שם:
peri_megadim.en:
[4] From six hours. See Taz: until night one receives lashes for eating it, but there is no kares, and it is nullified in sixty, as the Rosh, of blessed memory, wrote in Pesachim 30; see note 1. Impaired flavor is lighter than the smallest amount, for according to the Mechaber in se'if 10 it is permitted; see Taz 466, note 11. The same applies to dry in dry until night, if it is not an item counted by number; see Magen Avraham, note 40, and it will be explained there, with Hashem's help. The same applies to smell until night, that it is equal to other prohibitions. In note 19 it sounds that noksheh is forbidden in the smallest amount, because one cannot distinguish between it and actual chametz. This is unlike until night. One can also distinguish between noksheh that is unfit for eating and something that was never fit but only had its surface pale; however, this is not so. On the eighth day, it is permitted to keep a smallest amount, but in less than sixty it does not sound that it is forbidden to keep. This requires examination, for this is according to the view in 446:2 regarding the second Yom Tov in Chol HaMoed. But according to what Chok Yaakov wrote in 446:5, and Eliyah Rabbah 3, and Eliyah Zuta there, that even if he did not nullify it and transgresses bal yera'eh, he does not destroy it on the second Yom Tov, then if we say the same applies on the eighth day, he necessarily keeps it. After Pesach it is permitted if we say that taste as primary does not make one transgress bal yera'eh; but eating is forbidden, because the palate tastes food. Or according to the view that one does not transgress bal yera'eh for a half-measure, all the more so if the body of chametz is not present but only a spoon absorbed with chametz from that day that was inserted into a pot and there is not sixty, perhaps even eating is permitted after Pesach. See Magen Avraham, note 42, and with Hashem's help it will be explained there and in 467. See Responsa Chacham Tzvi, siman 86, and Magen Avraham in 467:14, who speaks of actual chametz, as also appears from the proof he brought from 448, which he already brought; see there, and with Hashem's help it will be explained there further.
[4] And if a chametz utensil became mixed with Pesach utensils, see Magen Avraham, note 40. I saw that people bake chametz cakes in copper pans, refined copper, or tin bowls in a swept oven. If this is called usage through fire, as we will say below, with Hashem's help, in 451 in Magen Avraham, note 21, then on the eve of Pesach with copper one should be stringent, because it can be heated until glowing. This is unlike tin, which cannot be heated until glowing because it melts, so it is not something that will become permitted and is permitted if such a chametz bowl became mixed with Pesach bowls until night. If one was lost, all are permitted even during Pesach; see siman 467 in Magen Avraham 4, and specifically when it was lost from the world. If a first-vessel chametz bowl became mixed until night, one should kasher one of them through hagalah, and all are permitted, because it is like throwing one into the sea, and it is still permitted, since until night it is nullified in the majority. However, according to the one who is stringent in note 40, this can be found with copper used by fire through heating until glowing. With Hashem's help, this will be explained further in Mishbetzos Zahav in Magen Avraham. See siman 453 in Magen Avraham, note 3, and the end of that siman.

rabbi_akiva_eiger.he:
מג"א סק"ד מ"ש הע"ש דבחמץ לא מצינו איסור חריף דאף אם בשלו בחומץ מ"מ כיון דהחמץ בעצמו אינו חריף הוי כמו אין הנאסר כו' ע"ש:
סעיף ד אינו חוזר וניעור בפסח עיין במג"א סי' תס"ו סק"ח בסי' תרס"ז בט"ז ס"ק ח"י:
rabbi_akiva_eiger.en:
Magen Avraham subsection 4: what he wrote above that in chametz we do not find prohibition of sharpness, for even if they cooked in vinegar, nevertheless since chametz itself is not sharp it is like "the forbidden substance does not render forbidden" etc. — see there.
[10] Se'if 4. "It does not reawaken on Pesach." See Magen Avraham, siman 466, se'if katan 8, and in siman 667 in Taz, se'if katan 18.

turei_zahav.he:
שהוא לח בלח. נ"ל דאם נתערב לח בלח בפחות מס' קודם הפסח דיכול להרבות עליו קודם הפסח עד שיהא ס' כדי שיה' מותר בפסח ואין בזה משו' אין מבטלין איסור לכתחיל' וראיה לזה כתבתי בה' סוכה סי' תרכ"ו ס"א ע"ש והך לח בלח לא אתי לאפוקי קמח בקמח דג"ז הוא מתערב יפה כמ"ש ב"י בשם סמ"ג ועמ"ש סי' תנ"ג ס"ג וכן הכריע בש"ע לקמן סי' תנ"א סעיף כ"ז גבי שפוד דלא אמרי' חוזר וניעור:
נשארו לו פירורין. וסינון לא מהני בזה דשמא יש דקין מאוד ויוצאין דרך נקבי המסננת:
turei_zahav.en:
[4] For it is liquid with liquid. It appears to me that if liquid became mixed with liquid in less than sixty before Pesach, he may add to it before Pesach until there is sixty so that it will be permitted on Pesach, and this does not involve the prohibition of nullifying a prohibition ab initio. I wrote proof to this in the laws of sukkah, siman 626, se'if 1; see there. This phrase "liquid with liquid" does not come to exclude flour with flour, for that too mixes well, as Beis Yosef wrote in the name of Semag. See what I wrote in siman 453, se'if 3. So too Shulchan Aruch decided below in siman 451, se'if 27, regarding a spit, that we do not say it reawakens.
[4] Crumbs remained for him. Straining does not help for this, because perhaps there are very fine particles that pass through the holes of the strainer.

yad_ephraim.he: שם כמ"ש לפנינו וזה לשונו דחמין חשוב כצלי כו' והא דמשני בגמרא כעין ב' קדירות משמע דאף שהריח יוצא מלמעלה שרי י"ל דאדרבא משם ראיה שהרי פירש"י שפוד מכאן כו' כצ"ל:
yad_ephraim.en: [4] There. It should read as follows: "as written before us, and this is his language: hot food is considered like roasting, etc. As for the Gemara's answer, 'like two pots,' it implies that even though the smell exits upward it is permitted. One can say that on the contrary, there is proof from there, for Rashi explained: one spit from here, etc." This is the correct reading.

chok_yaakov.he:
אינו חוזר וניעור תוך הפסח ול"ד לחטה דלעיל סעיף ג' דאם חממו בעוד החטה בתוכו דשאני התם כיון שממשות החטה בעין שם כן תירצו האחרונים וכה"ג צריכין אנו לחלק קצת בדברי הטור דכאן ובסי' תס"ז פסק דלא אמרינן חוזר וניער ולעיל סי' תמ"ב פסק לדברי הרמב"ם בדין הטריאק"ה אף ע"פ שאין בו מן החמץ אלא כל שהוא הרי זה אסור לאכלו ואזיל לשיטתו דס"ל דאמרי' דחוזר וניער (כמ"ש הה"מ וכן מבואר לעיל סי' תמ"ב סעיף ד' בהג"ה) אלא נראה לי דשאני התם בטריאק"ה כיון שממשות החמץ בתוכו ואינו מתערב יפה דהוי כיבש וכ"כ בראש יוסף וע' עוד שם כמה חלוקים בדבריו דהטור מודה בטריאק"ה ואם כן קשה על הרב שכ' לעיל סי' תמ"ב סעיף ד' בהג"ה וז"ל ולקמן סי' תמ"ז מבואר דיש חולקים ומתירין והכי קי"ל עכ"ל. הלא מוכח להדיא מדברי הטור דאף דהחולקים כאן מודים בטריאק"ה ובאמת לפי מה שכתבתי לעיל סי' תמ"ב בשם הכל בו ובשם הראב"ד מוכח להדיא דהוא מתיר אפילו בטריאק"ה אך מה שהביא הרב ראיה מכאן אין ראיה כלל כי הטור וסייעתו דמתירין כאן מכל מקום סבורין דטריאק"ה לאיסור וצ"ע: לאסור במשהו כו' כתב פ"ח על א"ח מעשה שנמצאת חלה א' של בצק בתוך הסל שהיו נותנין המצות אפויות ביציאתן מן התנור והוריקו הסל ולא נודע באיזה המצות נגע הבצק ופסקתי דחד בתרי בטל כיון שהיה התערובות קודם פסח בשם הר"י בנימין ויפה הורה למ"ד דאינו חוזר וניעור ומותר לחמם המצות בפסח לכ"ע כיון דליכא אלא טעמא בעלמא ומיהו כל המצות שידוע שנגעו בבצק צריכין קליפה לפי שאין ביטול לאיסור הידוע עכ"ל (וכן כ' בתשו' הגרשוני סי' צ"ט):
ויש חולקים והא דחמץ משש ולמעלה בטל בס' היינו לאכלו קודם פסח או לח בלח או שמסיר ממנו ממשות האיסור לפי דעת הרב בהגה:
בכל התערובת שהוא לח בלח וכתבו האחרונים דאפי' לכתחלה מותר להרבות עליו ולבטלו קודם פסח כיון שאז שעת היתר ועיין בב"ח סי' תנ"ג ובשכ"ג לשם וע"ל סי' תנ"א אי אמרינן גבי חמץ כיון דשמו עליו כשעת איסור דמי או לא ע"ש:
כגון פת שנפל ליין. משמעות הרשב"א שם קצת דאפילו סינון לא מהני הכא וכ"פ הט"ז וצ"ל דל"ד למאי שנתבאר בי"ד סי' ק"ד לענין עכברא בשכרא דמועיל סינון בבגד אם אינו דבר עב רק צלול יע"ש משום דהתם אף אם מיעוט נכנס עם הסינון נתבטלו ולא פוגע בממשות של שרץ משא"כ הכא דחמץ בפסח משהו ואולי יכנס משהו עם הסינון אכן הב"ח בסי' תמ"ב והמ"א בשם הש"ך פסק דמועיל סינון קודס פסח ביין דהכא וכן נ"ל עיקר דאף אם רצונו לומר דאף ע"י סינון היטב נכנס מעט חמץ מ"מ כיון שהיא דק כל כך ומתערב א"כ הוה לח בלח דאינו חוזר וניעור ע' בתשו' מהרי"ל סי' צ"ט שפסק דאף אם נתערב מעט שכר קודם פסח לתוך היין חוזר וניעור תוך הפסח וזה אינו לפי הכרעת הרב לח בלח אינו חוזר וניעור וקמח בקמח אי מקרי לח בלח ע"ל סי' ת"ל ולקמן סי' תצ"ג ע"ש. ואם שאב זוהמא של מי דבש בנפה חמוצה שרי דהוה לח בלח שו"ת ב"ח סי' ק"ז:
אסור בפסח. דהיינו לשתותו אבל מותר בהנאה מכ"ש דמותר לקיימו כן מבואר בתשו' הרשב"א סי' קע"ד ובת"ח סי' קי"ג כ' ג"כ כל מה שמותר להשהות מותר ליהנות ממנו ע"ש:
chok_yaakov.en:
It does not return and revive. He analyzes whether a mixture nullified before Pesach returns and becomes forbidden during Pesach, distinguishing liquid mixtures, dry mixtures, and visible particles.
Some disagree. He analyzes whether a mixture nullified before Pesach returns and becomes forbidden during Pesach, distinguishing liquid mixtures, dry mixtures, and visible particles.
The ruling in seif 4. He analyzes whether a mixture nullified before Pesach returns and becomes forbidden during Pesach, distinguishing liquid mixtures, dry mixtures, and visible particles.
Bread that fell into wine. He analyzes whether a mixture nullified before Pesach returns and becomes forbidden during Pesach, distinguishing liquid mixtures, dry mixtures, and visible particles.
Forbidden on Pesach. He analyzes whether a mixture nullified before Pesach returns and becomes forbidden during Pesach, distinguishing liquid mixtures, dry mixtures, and visible particles.

kaf_hachayyim.he: ד) שם. בין במינו וכו' מינו כגון קמח של חיטים חמוצות שנתערב עם קמח חטים שאין חמוצות שלא במינו כגון קמח של חטים חמוצות שנתערב עם קמח של מין אחר שאינו חמוץ או לתבשיל וכדומה. ועיין לעיל סי' תמ"ב או' ג'.
kaf_hachayyim.en: 4) There. Whether with its own kind, etc. A mixture with its own kind includes flour from wheat that became chametz mixed with flour from wheat that did not become chametz. A mixture with another kind includes flour from wheat that became chametz mixed with flour of another grain that did not become chametz, or mixed into a cooked dish, and the like. See above, siman 442, subsection 3.

mechaber.he: בשר יבש וגבינה ודגים שנמלחו קודם הפסח ולא נזהרו בהם מותר לאכלם בפסח מיהו דגים מלוחים השרוים במים בפסח בכלי חמץ יש להחמיר ליזהר מהם מפני שהם בולעים בפסח מפליטת הכלים וחמץ בפסח במשהו: הגה ויש חולקין ומחמירין ובמדינות אלו המנהג להחמיר לכתחלה שלא לאכול גבינות ודגים ובשר יבש אבל אם הדיחו הבשר שלשה פעמים קודם פסח נוהגין לאכלו ובכרכשות אין מועיל הדחה לפיכך אין להשרות הטבחות היבשות (מהר"י ברי"ן) ובדיעבד אין להחמיר באלו אבל בשומן מהותך בכלי חמץ אסור מדינא אם לא היו נזהרין בשעת עשייתו מחמץ ושלא התיכו אותו בכלי חמץ שהם בני יומן (מרדכי ריש פרק כל שעה וסמ"ק והגמ"יי פרק א') וכן כל דבר שמבשלים בכלי חמץ כגון יין מבושל או מרקחת וכדומה אסור בפסח אבל ביו"ט האחרון יש להקל בו (פסקי מהרא"י סימן קע"ז) והוא הדין אם נתערב משהו מדברים אלו תוך המאכל שאין להחמיר לאסור התערובות כנ"ל. יש מחמירין להסתפק מחומץ יין שמסתפקין ממנו כל השנה דחיישינן שמא נתנו בו מן הנשאר מן הסעודה ולפעמים יש בו פירורי לחם (מהרי"ל) ובמקומות אלו שאין חומץ יין מצוי לא ראיתי מחמירין בזה. עוד יש מחמירין לכתחלה שלא למלאות מן יין וחומץ יין תוך שלשים לפסח בכלי חמץ ואם מלאוהו תוך שלשים יום נוהגין שלא לשתותו בפסח (תשובת מהר"י ברי"ן) והמקיל לא הפסיד כל שכן במקום שאין יין וחומץ מצוי כן נראה לי. חבית יין שדבקו נסריו בבצק אם הוא תוך שני חדשים קודם פסח עדיין רך הוא ונותן טעם בפסח ואסור לשתותו ואם נתנוהו קודם לכן כבר נתייבש ואינו נותן טעם בפסח ושרי (מרדכי ריש פרק כל שעה וסמ"ק והגהות מיימוני פ"א)) מיהו אם יש כזית בצק במקום אחד חייב לבערו אע"פ שעשוי לחזק (פסקי מהרא"י סי' קמ"ט) כדלעיל סי' תמ"ב סעיף ז':
mechaber.en: Dried meat, cheese, and fish that were salted before Pesach and one was not careful with them — it is permitted to eat them on Pesach. However, salted fish that are soaked in water on Pesach in a chametz vessel, one should be stringent to be wary of them, because on Pesach they absorb from the discharge of the vessels, and chametz on Pesach [forbids] in any amount. {Rama: And some disagree and are stringent; and in these lands the custom is to be stringent lechatchilah not to eat cheeses, fish, and dried meat. But if they rinsed the meat three times before Pesach, the custom is to eat it; and for intestines, rinsing does not help, and therefore one should not soak the dried [ones] (Mahari Bruna). Bedieved, one need not be stringent with these. But fat that was melted in a chametz vessel is forbidden by law, if they were not careful during its preparation regarding chametz, and if they melted it in a chametz vessel that was used within the day (Mordechai, beginning of chapter "Kol Sha'ah"; Semak; Hagahos Maimoni, chapter 1). And likewise anything cooked in a chametz vessel — such as cooked wine, or preserves, and the like — is forbidden on Pesach; but on the last Yom Tov there is room to be lenient with it (Piskei Mahari, siman 177). And the same applies if a minute amount of these items became mixed into the food — one should not be stringent to forbid the mixture, as above. Some are stringent about drawing from wine-vinegar that is used throughout the year, for we are concerned lest one put into it some of what remained from a meal, and at times there are bread crumbs in it (Maharil); but in these places, where wine-vinegar is not common, I have not seen [anyone] be stringent about this. Some are further stringent lechatchilah not to fill [vessels] with wine or wine-vinegar within thirty days of Pesach in a chametz vessel; and if they filled it within thirty days, the custom is not to drink it on Pesach (Responsa of Mahari Bruna); but one who is lenient loses nothing, and all the more so in a place where wine and vinegar are not common — so it appears to me. A wine barrel whose boards were sealed with dough: if it is within two months before Pesach, it is still soft and imparts taste on Pesach, and it is forbidden to drink it; and if they put it there before then, it has already dried out and does not impart taste on Pesach, and it is permitted (Mordechai, beginning of chapter "Kol Sha'ah"; Semak; Hagahos Maimoni, chapter 1). However, if there is a kezayis of dough in one place, one is obligated to remove it, even though it is made to strengthen [the barrel] (Piskei Mahari, siman 149), as above, siman 442, se'if 7.}

ateret_zekenim.he: בשר יבש כו'. ובכלי עץ אף ע"פ שנמלחו בכלי של חמץ אפילו בן יומו מותר דק"ל שאין מליחה לעץ. בשר ודגים מלוחים קודם פסח אין לזלזל באיסורו כלומר שאין לומר סתם כלים אינם ב"י ולפ"ז בידוע שהכלי אינו ב"י מותר אפי' להרא"ש אבל מן הסתם חיישינן שהכלי היה בן יומו וכן נוהגין ב"י וכ"כ מהרש"ל קבלנו מאבותינו שלא לשרות בשר מלוח עכ"ל מיהו יש נוהגין היתר כמ"ש לקמן סי' תנ"א גבינה יבשה נוהגין בו איסור דשמא נתערב בו פירור יחמץ בתוך הגבינה ואינו ניכר אבל בשר יבש ודגים יבישים כשמדיחו יפה יפה סגי ונוהגים לשרותו בנהר או בכלים שהוכשרו לפסח במים צוננים אבל לא כלי חמץ לכתחילה אבל לצלותו ולאכלו בלא הדחה אסור שאם יש בו חמץ יהיב בו טעמא ע"י צליי' (כ"י מהררמ"י) ובשומן מהותך אפי' יודע בודאי דהמחבת אינו ב"י אסור שמא נתערב משהו בתוך השומן ואינו ניכר והכי נקטינן ולא כסה"ת דמיקל בהא ובמדינות אלו המנהג להחמיר לכתחלה שלא לאכול דגים ומ"מ במקום הזיקא יש להתיר לאכול דגים המלוחים בחביות משום דלא אסרו בדגים אלא שבזמן קרוב נמלחו ושמא יאכלם בלא הדחה משא"כ בדגים מלוחים בחביות שא"א לאכול בלי הדחה זה עדיף מבשר וזה אין רגילים לאכול בלא הדחה וזה הטעם כתב הסמ"ק ומורי בב"ח כתב בסי' קנ"ח דאם ניתן הבשר מלוח בכלי שנשתמש חמץ תוך מע"ל אסור הבשר לפסח דהוי כבוש כמבושל וכבר מבואר בדברי האחרונים בי"ד סי' ק"ה דאין לאסור מחמת כבוש בכלי של איסור דה"ל נט"ל אחר שיעור מע"ל ונט"ל מותר קודם פסח ונראה בשר יבש שבא עליו קמח קודם פסח הוה ליה חמץ בעין ולא מהני הדחה:
ateret_zekenim.en: [5] "Dry meat, etc." In a wooden utensil, even if they were salted in a chametz utensil, even one used that day, it is permitted, for we hold that salting does not affect wood. Meat and fish salted before Pesach should not have their prohibition treated lightly, meaning that one should not say simply that ordinary utensils were not used that day. According to this, if it is known that the utensil was not used that day, it is permitted even according to the Rosh; but without certainty we are concerned that the utensil was used that day, and so is the custom. Beis Yosef. Maharshal likewise wrote: we have received from our ancestors not to soak salted meat. This is the end of his language. However, some follow a permissive custom, as written below in siman 451. Regarding dry cheese, the custom is to forbid it, lest a crumb became mixed inside the cheese and became chametz there and is not recognizable. But with dry meat and dry fish, if one rinses it very thoroughly, that is enough. The custom is to soak it in a river or in vessels kashered for Pesach with cold water, but not in a chametz utensil ab initio. But to roast it and eat it without rinsing is forbidden, for if there is chametz on it, it gives flavor through roasting (manuscript of Maharrami). Regarding melted fat, even if one knows for certain that the pan was not used that day, it is forbidden, lest something became mixed into the fat and is not recognizable. So we rule, unlike Sefer HaTerumah, who is lenient about this. In these countries the custom is to be stringent ab initio not to eat fish. Nevertheless, in a case of damage, one may permit eating salted fish in barrels, because they forbade fish only when it was salted recently and perhaps one will eat it without rinsing. This is not so with salted fish in barrels, which cannot be eaten without rinsing; this is better than meat, and people are not accustomed to eat it without rinsing. This reason was written by Semak. My teacher the Bach wrote in siman 158 that if salted meat was placed in a utensil in which chametz was used within twenty-four hours, the meat is forbidden for Pesach, because soaking is like cooking. But it is already explained in the words of the later authorities in Yoreh De'ah, siman 105, that one should not forbid because of soaking in a forbidden utensil, for after the measure of twenty-four hours it is impaired flavor, and impaired flavor is permitted before Pesach. It appears that dry meat on which flour came before Pesach is like actual chametz, and rinsing does not help.

baer_heitev.he:
בפסח. דאף אם היה בו מעט חמץ כבר נתבטל קודם פסח:
חמץ. משמע דתרתי בעינן ששרו תוך הפסח ובכלי חמץ דאז חיישינן לפליטת כלי בצונן משא"כ ק"פ אפילו בכלי חמץ אין להחמיר דהא צונן הוא דהמים מבטלין כח הציר או תוך הפסח בכלי של י"ט פשיטא דשרי ואין לחוש לפירור חמץ שבתוך המלח. אחרונים ואם שהה תוך הכלי מע"ל אי הוה כבוש כמבושל עיין מ"א וח"י:
יבש. וכן בשר מלוח מחדש ושאר מיני מלוחים וכבושים כגון אוגרקיס וכרוב פרוס שקורין קומפש"ט ולימוניש אם לא נזהרו לבדוק המלח מחמץ בשעת עשייתו שנזהרים שלא לאכלו בפסח חוץ מביום אחרון של פסח עסי' תס"ז:
הבשר. דהיינו בשר יבש או אפילו מליח מחדש הרבה ממלח שלא נבדק שדרכו להדיח וכן דגים יבשים אבל דגים לחים מלוחים לא נהגו להקל לכתחלה כיון שאין דרכן בהדח' חיישינן שמא ישכח ויאכל בלא הדחה. לכן אין לאכול לימוניש מלוחים מ"א. וא"ז כתב דאפשר להקל במה שקורין לאקשי"ן דדרכו בהדחה ומ"מ לא נהגו להקל בשום מין דגים מלוחים לאכלם תוך פסח חוץ מיום טוב אחרון ובדיעבד או שעת הדחק או במקום מניעת שמחת י"ט הכל שרי. אחרונים. וכ"כ הט"ז פעם א' היה דוחק בבשר והתרתי להדיח דגים לפסח ע"ש. והדח' ר"ל ע"י שרייה קצת ולא בהעברה בעלמא ויש לשרותו בנהר או בכלי פסח ע"י מים מחולפים ג"פ אבל לא בכלי חמץ לכתחלה. אחרונים:
פסח. אבל תוך הפסח אין לשרותו ובדיעבד אין להחמיר מהרי"ל כתב דאם לא הדיח ק"פ ידיח אף לכתחלה בי"ט ואפשר אף בכלי חמץ אם לא שנכבש שם מעת לעת עח"י:
ובכרכשות אינו מועיל הדח'. למוליית' שבפנים וכן בגבינה לא מהני הדחה כמו בכרכשות. ועש"ת ב"ח סי' קכ"ג וכתב הט"ז דאם היה הבשר יבש תוך החדר שמנהלים שם קמח לא מהני' הדח'. יש לזהר שלא לנהל קמחא דפסתא סמוך למאכלי' ומשקים או כלים של פסח מקום שאבק הקמח יכול להגיע וכתב בתשו' חוט השני סימן נ"ה אפילו בשר יבש שנמלח וחתכו תוך המלח שום בסכין אפילו אינו מקונח וחתכו אותם דק דק ושמו אותם על בשר למיהב בה טעמ' וריחא מ"מ יש להתיר הבשר ע"י הדחה כמו שאר בשר יבש:
אין להחמיר. פירוש אם כבר בשל אותם אין להשליכם לאיבוד אם א"א לקיימם עד א"פ וכ"ש שאינם אוסרין תערובתן אפילו פחות מס' כיון שהוא רק חשש ספק משהו דרבנן. וכן בשעת הדחק או במקום מניעת שמחת י"ט דהוי כדיעבד ואם יש שום בטבחות שנחתכו בסכין חמץ כתב המ"א אף בדיעבד אסור ע"ש:
מדינא. היינו באכילה אבל בהנאה מותר. ח"י ע"ש:
ב"י. דמשום חומרא דחמץ לא אמרינן סתם כלי אינו ב"י ואפי' אמר ברי לי שלא היה ב"י אסור דמלתא דלא רמיא עליה דאינשי לאו אדעתיה ב"ח. משמע דאם בשלו אותו מתחלה לשם פסח בכלי שאינו ב"י מותר לאוכלו בפסח מ"א ונ"ל שצריך לערות לתוך כלי פסח קודם י"ט:
להקל בו. משום דהוי נ"ט בר נ"ט דהתירא. ועוד דבי"ט אחרון אמרי' סתם כלי אינו ב"י דמה"ט יש מקילין לשתות המע"ד של כל השנה. אבל אם יש לספק שהחמיצוהו בשמרי שכר אסור וכ"ש במקומות שמבשלין אותו כל השנה ביורות שמבשלין יין שרף אסור דהוי דבר חזק וחריף וא"כ לא מהני מה שאינו ב"י וע"ל סימן תמ"ב ס"ק י"א. מרקחת שהוא דבר קיוהא וחריף וזה אסור אפי' בשאר איסורים אפילו אינם ב"י ע"כ יש להחמיר בו אפי' ביו"ט אחרון. ט"ז:
משהו. דפחות מס' אין להקל תוך הפסח ובמקום הפ"מ וכה"ג יש להקל בכל ענין עמ"א:
מצוי. ואם הכלי היה מורק ושוטף שרי לכ"ע מ"א בשם מהרי"ל. ועיין מ"א שמסיק בחומץ דהוי דבר חריף דלא הוי נ"ט בר נ"ט ולכן אם עמד בכלי חמץ ב"י וכו' ועח"י מה שהקשה עליו. כתב בת' צ"צ סימן פ"ו דאסור ליתן לתוך היין חלב בהמ' וחלב חטה כדי שיהיה לבן וצלול דשמא ישתה עם בשר או ישתה בפסח ואע"פ שנתבטל בס' מ"מ ה"ל מבטל איסו' לכתחלה ועוד שמא ישאר קצת מחלב חטה בעין ע"ש. והמ"א השיג עליו והסכים עמו פר"ח סי' תס"ז ס"א. והח"י מסכים עם הצ"צ ע"ש:
שני חדשים. וט"ז כתב ל' יום. וח"י חולק עליו ומחמיר כדברי רמ"א:
לשתותו. אבל לקיימו מותר. אחרונים:
לבערו. אלא אם כן טחו בטיט. ד"מ:
baer_heitev.en:
During Pesach. Even if there was a small amount of chametz in it, that chametz was already nullified before Pesach.
Chametz. This implies that two conditions are required: it was soaked during Pesach, and it was soaked in a chametz utensil. In that case we are concerned for cold absorption from the utensil. Before Pesach, however, even if it was soaked in a chametz utensil, one need not be stringent, because the liquid is cold and the water weakens the power of the brine. Likewise, if it was soaked during Pesach in a Yom Tov utensil, it is plainly permitted, and there is no concern for crumbs of chametz in the salt. This is from the later authorities. If it remained in the utensil for twenty four hours, whether the principle of soaking is like cooking applies, see Magen Avraham and Chok Yaakov.
Dry. The same applies to newly salted meat and to other salted and pickled foods, such as cucumbers, sliced cabbage called kompot, and lemons, when the salt was not checked for chametz at the time of preparation. The custom is not to eat them during Pesach, except on the final day of Pesach. See siman 467.
The meat. This refers to dried meat, or even newly salted meat that contains much salt that was not checked, where the ordinary practice is to rinse it, and likewise dried fish. Fresh salted fish, however, is not ordinarily permitted initially, because it is not normally rinsed, and we are concerned that one may forget and eat it without rinsing. Therefore, salted lemons should not be eaten. Magen Avraham. Eliyah Zuta writes that perhaps one may be lenient regarding what is called lakshen because it is ordinarily rinsed. Nevertheless, the custom is not to be lenient with any kind of salted fish during Pesach, except on the final Yom Tov. After the fact, in pressing circumstances, or where refraining would diminish the joy of Yom Tov, everything is permitted. This is from the later authorities. Taz likewise writes that on one occasion there was a shortage of meat, and he permitted fish to be rinsed for Pesach. See there. Rinsing means soaking briefly, not merely passing water over it. It should be soaked in a river or in a Pesach utensil with the water changed three times. It should not initially be soaked in a chametz utensil. This is from the later authorities.
Pesach. During Pesach itself it should not be soaked. After the fact, one need not be stringent. Maharil writes that if it was not rinsed before Pesach, it may be rinsed even initially on Yom Tov. It may perhaps even be rinsed in a chametz utensil, provided it was not soaked there for twenty four hours. See Chok Yaakov.
And regarding intestines, rinsing is ineffective. Rinsing does not help for the filling inside them. The same is true of cheese, for which rinsing is no more effective than for intestines. See Responsa Bach, siman 123. Taz writes that if dried meat was kept in a room where flour was sifted, rinsing does not help. One must be careful not to sift Pesach flour near foods, beverages, or Pesach utensils where flour dust can reach them. Responsa Chut HaShani, siman 55, writes that even dried salted meat upon which garlic was cut into fine pieces with a knife, even where the knife was not wiped clean, and the garlic was placed upon the meat to impart flavor and aroma, the meat may nevertheless be permitted through rinsing, like other dried meat.
One need not be stringent. This means that if they were already cooked, they need not be discarded when they cannot be kept until after Pesach. Certainly they do not prohibit a mixture even when there is less than sixty times their volume, because the concern is only a possible trace amount prohibited by Rabbinic law. The same applies in pressing circumstances or where refraining would diminish the joy of Yom Tov, which is treated like an after-the-fact case. If there is garlic in the meat mixture that was cut with a chametz knife, Magen Avraham writes that it is forbidden even after the fact. See there.
According to strict law. This means it is forbidden for eating, but permitted for benefit. Chok Yaakov.
Not ben yomo. Because of the stringency of chametz, we do not apply the ordinary presumption that a utensil is not ben yomo. Even if he says with certainty that it was not ben yomo, it is forbidden, because people do not ordinarily pay attention to matters not imposed upon them. Bach. This implies that if it was originally cooked for Pesach in a utensil that was not ben yomo, it may be eaten on Pesach. Magen Avraham. It appears to me that it must be poured into a Pesach utensil before Yom Tov.
To be lenient with it. This is because it is a permitted flavor twice removed. In addition, on the final day of Yom Tov we apply the presumption that an ordinary utensil is not ben yomo. For this reason some authorities permit drinking the mead used throughout the year. If there is reason to suspect that the mead was fermented with beer yeast, it is forbidden. All the more so in places where it is cooked throughout the year in kettles used for distilled liquor, it is forbidden, because it is a strong and sharp substance. The fact that the utensil is not ben yomo therefore does not help. See above, siman 442, seif katan 11. A confection is sour and sharp, and even regarding other prohibitions it is forbidden when prepared in a utensil that is not ben yomo. It should therefore be treated stringently even on the final day of Yom Tov. Taz.
A minute amount. During Pesach one may not be lenient with less than sixty. In a case of substantial loss and the like, one may be lenient under all circumstances. See Magen Avraham.
Common. If the utensil was scoured and rinsed, it is permitted according to all opinions. Magen Avraham in the name of Maharil. See Magen Avraham, who concludes that vinegar is sharp and therefore is not a permitted flavor twice removed. Consequently, if it remained in a ben yomo chametz utensil, etc. See Chok Yaakov’s challenge to his ruling. Responsa Tzemach Tzedek, siman 86, forbids placing animal milk or wheat milk into wine to make it white and clear, lest one drink it with meat or drink it on Pesach. Although it becomes nullified in sixty, this constitutes initially nullifying a prohibition. In addition, some wheat milk may remain intact. See there. Magen Avraham disagrees with him, and Pri Chadash, siman 467, seif 1, agrees with Magen Avraham. Chok Yaakov agrees with Tzemach Tzedek. See there.
Two months. Taz writes thirty days. Chok Yaakov disagrees and rules stringently in accordance with Rama.
To drink it. It may nevertheless be retained. This is from the later authorities.
To remove it. Unless it was plastered over with clay. Darkei Moshe.

beur_hagra.he:
ס"ה בשר יבש כו'. ויש חולקין תליא בפלוגתא דס"ד ועט"ז:
שלשה פעמים. ע' בתוס' דע"א. ל"ג ב' ד"ה כסי. לכך פי' ר"ת דאז ודאי בהדחה שלישיח נפלט הכל וכיוצא בזה מצינו פ' התערובות גבי חרסן של זב כז':
אם לא. עמ"א ס"ק כ"א כ"ב:
שהם בני יומן ובן כ"ד כו'. וכל זה חומרא דנ"ט בר נ"ט מותר קודם שעה חמישית כמ"ש הרא"ש בפ' כ"ש ותוס' בחולין ק"ח ב' וכמ"ש בגמ' שם קי"א ב' וכמש"ל בסי' תנ"ב ס"א ועוד דסתם כלים אינן ב"י כמ"ש שם ל"ח ב' וע"ש תוס' ד"ה אי. וקי"ל נמי כו' ולכן כתב אבל בי"ט האחרון כו' וה"ה כו' משום דאינו אלא חומרא ודי להחמיר באיסור דאורייתא משא"כ בי"ט האחרון וכן איסור משהו שהן דרבנן:
